newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-PAKISTAN TIED DOWN BY SRI LANKAN BOWLERS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN TIED DOWN BY SRI LANKAN BOWLERS.

text.p: Pakistan, tied down by some accurate bowling by Sri Lanka, added only 33 runs in the post-tea session before play was called off due to poor light on the second day of the second and final test on Sunday.
Inzamam-ul Haq and Asif Mujtaba kept their wickets but the score moved slowly before play was halted with Pakistan on 146 for 4 in reply to Sri Lanka's first-innings total of 331.
Inzamam, usually known for his flamboyant batting, crawled to an unbeaten 43 in 167 minutes while Mujtaba battled through 138 minutes for his 32.
The two came together when Pakistan were 83 for 4 and they had added 63 runs for the fifth wicket at close of play.
Neither batsman was able to get over the accurate bowling of Sri Lankan spin duo Ruwan Kalpage and Russell Arnold, who were well supported by Chaminda Vaas.
Kalpage, who replaced the injured Muthiah Muralitharan, reeled off 16 overs, giving away only 19 runs. Arnold's five overs cost just two runs.
Pakistan found themselves struggling early as Vaas and Sajeeva de Silva took two wickets each.
Vaas claimed Salim Elahi and Ijaz Ahmed to send Pakistan reeling at 13 for 2. De Silva chipped in with the prize wickets of captain Rameez Raja and Salim Malik to put the visitors on the defensive.
Earlier Aravinda de Silva, who on Saturday held Sri Lanka together with a stylish century, continued where he had left off when Sri Lanka resumed at their overnight 271 for 7.
He was left unbeaten on 138 and his 208-ball innings contained 15 boundaries. He and Vaas (17) added 76 runs for the eighth wicket, a record for Sri Lanka.
For Pakistan, Saqlain Mushtaq was the pick of the bowlers after he claimed four Sri Lankan wickets for 115 runs, taking his series tally to 13 wickets.
